messages:
jordan_sales: Hey team — we have a POC next Tue 09:00-12:00 UTC for AcmeCorp. They expect a demo traffic spike and asked for a hosted API rate bump. Current default keys are too low. Can we provision a scoped key + temporary QPS increase?

divya_se: Quick details pls — expected peak qps and avg tokens per request? Also need IP allowlist or ephemeral key?

jordan_sales: Peak ~180 qps, sustained ~120 qps, avg ~600 tokens/req (mostly chat completions). Window is 3 hrs but main demo is the first 45m. They’d like 200 qps headroom. Prefer scoped key pinned to the demo app + IP allowlist (customer will give IP ranges).

alexm: 200 qps of 600 tokens ≈ 120k tokens/sec, that’s large. Do they need streaming? Which model are they testing? If using a large model we should recommend a smaller quantized variant to hit latency/cost targets.

jordan_sales: They want flushed chat with streaming. Model: trying out "redwood-instruct-13b" in hosted catalog. We asked them to try a quantized 13b-8bit if available.

luis_eng: Recommend limiting concurrency per-key + a soft limit rather than hard unlimited bump. We can enable a temporary policy: 220 qps soft cap with token-based throttling fallback. That avoids global overload and gives them bursts.

divya_se: Also confirm billing — temporary increases during POC are usually covered by demo credits, but if they exceed credits we bill at hosted overage rates. Jordan, confirm with sales ops and put ceiling on spend.

jordan_sales: Will do, putting $2k demo ceiling.

infra-bot: To proceed create an internal ticket with the following fields: customer, demo window (UTC), scoped_key_name, ip_allowlist (CIDR), qps_request, spend_ceiling. Use template: `/ops ticket create --type rate-adjust --customer "AcmeCorp" --start 2026-03-31T09:00Z --end 2026-03-31T12:00Z --qps 220 --notes "scoped key + ip allowlist + spend cap $2000"`

alexm: Once ticket is created I can attach a temporary policy + generate the scoped key. For IP allowlist we’ll need the CIDRs at least 24h before the demo.

divya_se: Also tell them to enable client-side batching and prefix caching to reduce token load. Example: use streaming with incremental commits and reduce max_tokens where possible.

jordan_sales: Acme said they can drop max_tokens to 512 for demo requests. Should be fine.

infra-bot: Ticket created: OPS-4582 (link: https://redwood.internal/ops/OPS-4582). Scheduling temporary soft cap 220 qps from 2026-03-31T09:00Z -> 2026-03-31T12:00Z. Scoped key will be generated and posted to vault. Please supply CIDRs before 2026-03-30T09:00Z.

alexm: When OPS-4582 is approved I’ll run the change. Command I’ll use to create scoped key (example):
```
redwoodctl keys create --name "acme-demo-2026-03-31" --scopes "models:use,rls:scoped" --restrict-ips "203.0.113.0/24,198.51.100.0/24" --expires "2026-04-01T00:00Z"
```

divya_se: Thanks — can you also add a small dashboard (per-route qps/token-rate) and an alert at 85% of soft cap? We want to see it live during the demo.

alexm: Yup, will add a Grafana panel and a pager alert to the sales ops channel but set to notify only if they hit 95% for >2m.

jordan_sales: Awesome. Acme — I’ll confirm CIDRs and spend cap now. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Change scheduled and will auto-revert to baseline at 2026-04-01T00:00Z unless extended via OPS ticket.
